title: From All That Dwell Below the Skies
description: From All That Dwell Below the Skies in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 117, part 2.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: From all that dwell be-low the skies, Let the Cre-a-tor's praise a-rise! Let the Re-deem-er's name be sung Thro' ev-ery land, by ev-ery tongue.

lines: From all that dwell below the skies,
Let the Redeemer's name be sung
Thro' every land, by every tongue.
Thy praise shall sound from shore to shore,
Till suns shall rise and set no more.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
